chapter_title: The Chapter of the Three Seasons
chapter_note: This kephalaion is dominated by systematic cosmological time-structuring (three seasons: descent/ascent of the First Man; ordering of the universe; final redemptive span from the Ambassador’s Image to the ascent of the Statue). The only clear later material is the dialogue frame apparatus ("apostle", "disciples" Q&A attributions), which wraps or punctuates otherwise core teaching. No NT citation formulae or institutional/pastoral grafts appear; “Jesus” here reads as the mythic/cosmic saviour-agent within the Manichaean system rather than a Gospel overlay.

paragraphs.core_text: From the time when the Light came forth and was crucified in the Darkness, to the season when the Statue will ascend and the entire Light, which was conjoined with the Darkness, will be purified and cleansed. From that time on, from that time to the season of the end totals three seasons.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution and speaker tag ("Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:" and "He says:") as later hagiographic compilation apparatus.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core content is a global three-time schema (Light–Darkness mixture → purification/end) stated impersonally; the only late signals are the explicit ‘apostle → disciples’ dialogue framing.

paragraphs.core_text: Three seasons: from the time when the First Man went down to the abyss, and waged the war and the struggle against the King of the realms of Darkness and his other powers. He was victorious, while his sons remain behind with them in the worlds [... ...] in the [...] until he shall catch all of them [...] he bound them all up, so that not one of them escaped his hand. He won a great victory [... ...] The First Man spent human lifetimes and generations in the land of darkness, until he prevailed [...] ⟨p.56⟩ he fulfilled the will of the greatness that was commanded of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic mythic chronology anchored in core cosmic actors (First Man, King of Darkness) and process (war/struggle, binding, victory) with no institutional ‘pointing-at’.

paragraphs.core_text: Then they sent the Living Spirit, the Father of Life. He brought the First Man up from the struggle, he brought him up to the land of light. This is the first period, from the descent of the First Man to his ascent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic core cosmological rescue sequence and explicit period delimitation; impersonal ‘this is the first period’ structuring marks the substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The second season is from the time when the First Man ascended. The Living Spirit came, and the Mother of Life. They set in order the things of the universe, they set up [...] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living set in order [...] the universe, up to the moment when they go out [...] it was reckoned to the second season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos exposition: divine hypostases ordering the universe; explicit temporal boundary (‘reckoned to the second season’) is characteristic of the systematic layer.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] the universe [...] the Third Ambassador spread [...] that is in the [...] living; he [...] he separated beauty from all the powers and scooped it up to the heights, he swept the waste to the abyss, and he [... ...] Now, from the moment when the Ambassador revealed his image he purified the light. Sin spurted up towards him. He hid his image. Sin came [...] from the Darkness. It sculpted the trees and the abortions fell down. Afterwards they sculpted Adam and Eve in the flesh. Until the moment when Jesus was sent and he [...] as he performed there his will. He gave the hope to Adam, and ascended to the heights.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological sequence remains internal to the Manichaean system (Ambassador’s Image, Sin as a cosmic agent, creation of Adam/Eve, salvific sending/ascension). No Gospel citation or ecclesial application language appears.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, from the time when the Ambassador displayed his image until the season when the Statue will ascend at the end, shall be reckoned to the third season.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure period-definition formula closing the three-season schema; no frame or pastoral intrusion.
Dialogue connector (‘disciples asked the apostle’) with no substantive teaching content preserved; typical compilational frame punctuation.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] ⟨p.57⟩ [...] lasts long in the time that the First Man spent in the world of Darkness. It is a very great count of time, more than the (other) two seasons!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (‘The apostle says to them’) as later frame; retained the comparative temporal teaching that follows.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is comparative time-measure within the three-season system; the ‘apostle says’ tag is a later Q&A wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: The first season, which the First Man spent in the world of Darkness, is how much longer than the time that this universe has been? While it is established?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (‘His disciples say to him:’) while retaining the substantive cosmological question.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Question is about internal cosmological chronology (duration of First Man’s darkness-period vs. universe-time). The Q&A framing is later editorial apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: If you should say that [... ...] it is small, if you should [... ...] to him [...] and you consult [...] you will tell him: Twenty times! It is greater again in this other one that you will consult: Thirty times! Less also is this other one [... ...] people will receive the {} of the trees [... ...] the years and the generations [...] earth to the heights. This is [...
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed bracketed reply attribution (‘[He replies to them]:’) as frame material; kept the comparative ‘consult / twenty times / thirty times’ teaching sequence.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite second-person rhetoric, the content functions as an internal cosmological comparison of durations rather than pastoral exhortation; the explicit reply tag is a later dialogue wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the third period, from the time when the Ambassador revealed his image until the Statue will ascend from the lump. It again, that time, is greater than the intermediate; but it does not come equal to the time of the First Man. For this intermediate season, in which the Father of Life and the Mother of Life constructed the universe with its orders, is shorter than that of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal comparative chronology across the three seasons; fully internal cosmic referents and explicit period labels are substrate markers.

paragraphs.core_text: Great is the period of the First Man! It lasts longer than the season in which the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the world and the Statue ascends. From the time too when the Ambassador displayed his image, until the dissolution of the universe [... ...] when the Father of Life and the Mother of Life shaped the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative internal time-comparison; no institutional ‘application’ target—still cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the [...] three periods of time that occur. ⟨p.58⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief closure of the systematic three-period teaching; no frame doxology or church application.
